text: Magdalenenberg was a Continental Celtic archaeological site. In the early 1890s, and again in the 1970s, workers excavated a significant gravesite at Villingen-Schwenningen in Germany. The town stands near the original source of Celtic culture. One of the largest burial mounds in the region, it covered more than a hundred graves. The graves held many ritual and personal artifacts. Koch records it as a Hallstatt period tumulus, the largest in the west Hallstatt province. It measured about 102 meters in diameter and about 8 meters in height. Its burials date from around 625 to 550 B.C.E.
